blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from Jared's verified local notes (researched November 1, 2026). Listing-stated figures are labelled; unconfirmed items say so. No live feed filtered to 55+ homes yet.

In Upper Lonsdale, the 55+ homes you can buy are Somerset Green and Vista 29 (strata). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is retirement residence or care. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Upper Lonsdale
Somerset Green — 121 West 29th St (also fronting 2800 Chesterfield Ave), CITY of North Vancouver side

Freehold strata apartment complex on the south side of West 29th Street. A District of North Vancouver council report (Dec 22, 2004) describes it, from the District's side of the boundary, as "the existing 143 unit 'Somerset Green' seniors' condominium apartment development in the City of North Vancouver," with suites averaging approximately 102 m² (1,100 sq ft). Current listings (, Oct 2026) market it as a 55+ community and state the rule in occupancy terms: "Owner can be legal age, but one resident must be 55+." Amenities recorded in current listings: indoor pool, hot tub, workshop, gym/exercise room, library, games room, lounge, landscaped courtyard gardens and 2 guest suites; pets welcome / cats OK in listing data. A listing for a unit addressed as 201–2800 Chesterfield Ave describes the same Somerset Green complex, confirming the Chesterfield frontage. Build year: most current listings state 1987; one listing states 1989 — conflict flagged, 1987 is the majority figure. Strata plan number: Not confirmed from a citable source (do not rely on aggregator plan listings).
Vista 29 — 188 West 29th St, DISTRICT of North Vancouver side

Freehold strata, plan BCS2494, built 2007, on the block between West Queens Road and West 29th Street east of Chesterfield Avenue. An MLS feature sheet for the building records: Total Units in Strata: 50, zoning CD52, title Freehold Strata. Current listings (, Oct 2026) market it as an adult-oriented (55+) building and state "One owner to be 55+." The District's Dec 22, 2004 council report on this exact site (Harbourview Projects Corporation) proposed 50 dwelling units — 42 single-level condominium units in a four-storey apartment building plus 8 three-bedroom townhouses — with a restrictive covenant "to limit occupancy to households where one member is 55 years of age or older," in Comprehensive Development Zone 52 (CD 52); the as-built 50-unit count and CD52 zoning on the feature sheet match that approval. Amenities recorded in current listings: club/amenity room, guest suite (one listing states $35 per night — listing-stated, confirm with the strata), workshop, secure underground parking, 13 on-site visitor stalls, storage locker; pet friendly.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Upper Lonsdale (not for sale)

items.t: Chartwell Churchill House — 150 West 29th St: Private-pay rental retirement residence — rental suites with services, not strata ownership. Registered with BC's Assisted Living Registry as Chartwell Churchill House, legal operator Chartwell Master Care LP, class SN (seniors), at 150 West 29th Street, V7N 0A1. The operator describes it as a boutique-style, continuum-of-care residence offering both independent living and assisted living under one roof — which it calls the North Shore's only retirement residence offering both — with staff on-site 24-7, emergency response, and pet-friendly suites; suite types run from studio to two-bedroom. The operator locates it "at 29th Street West and Lonsdale Avenue — near W Queen Road and the Trans-Canada Highway" and states it is five minutes from Lions Gate Hospital. Unit/suite count: Not confirmed from a source that names this residence (a 2004 District report records the lots east of the Vista 29 site as rezoned for a 97-unit seniors' assisted-living development, but it does not name Churchill House, so the 97 figure is not attributed to it here).

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Upper Lonsdale

items.t: The sub-area runs up Lonsdale Avenue from about 24th/25th Street to Rockland Avenue, where Lonsdale ends. TransLink's North Shore Area Transit Plan jurisdiction table corroborates the split on the avenue itself: it assigns the Lonsdale Avenue at 29th Street layover to City jurisdiction and the Upper Lonsdale layovers at Osborne Avenue and at Prospect/Rockland to District jurisdiction.
Nearby areas: Central Lonsdale (south, City), Delbrook (northwest, District), Braemar and Tempe (east), Lynn Valley (northeast, District).

The commercial node is Queensdale, at Lonsdale Avenue and Queens Road — one of the six Village Centres designated in the District's OCP, described as providing a range of shops and services for daily needs. Full-service shopping is down the hill in Central Lonsdale.

Schools serving the sub-area are in School District 44 for both municipalities: Westview Elementary and Larson Elementary (K–7; Larson, at 2605 Larson Road, is dual-track English and French Immersion), École André-Piolat (francophone K–12, 380 West Kings Road), and Carson Graham Secondary (2145 Jones Avenue) for most addresses. Catchments are address-based — easternmost addresses should be checked against the Argyle boundary with SD44.

Transit: TransLink Route 230 runs the full length of Lonsdale Avenue from Lonsdale Quay to the top of Upper Lonsdale and down Rockland; the SeaBus crosses from the Quay to Waterfront Station in 12 minutes, every 15 minutes during the day and every 10 minutes at peak.
Highway 1 (Upper Levels) interchanges at Lonsdale and Westview give east–west highway access. No official drive-time figure is published — drive times not confirmed.

Where the 55+ housing actually concentrates: in one block only — the 100 block of West Queens Road / West 29th Street at Chesterfield Avenue, at the Queensdale node. All of the area's verified 55+ and seniors stock (Somerset Green, Vista 29, Chartwell Churchill House) sits in that block, which the District's own planning record designated for seniors' housing. The rest of Upper Lonsdale is predominantly single-detached houses climbing the slope, with no other 55+ complex verified.
Elevation: the top of Lonsdale at Rockland is often quoted at about 850 feet (259 m) above sea level — not confirmed, no City, District or other official source stating it was found.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Upper Lonsdale

items.t: Extra layer at Vista 29 — a covenant, not just a bylaw: The District's 2004 approval for the Vista 29 site included, as item 9 of the application, "a restrictive covenant to limit occupancy to households where one member is 55 years of age or older," alongside the CD 52 comprehensive development zoning. A buyer should have the covenant on title reviewed as well as the strata bylaws — the two are separate instruments.

CITY rules (south of 29th Street — Somerset Green block): the City of North Vancouver's Official Community Plan is the Official Community Plan, 2014, No. 8400, amended December 8, 2025 (Amendment Bylaw 2025, No. 9114) for provincial housing requirements. On Dec 8, 2025 the City also adopted the Ground Oriented (GO) Zone, increasing permitted units from 3 to 4 on nearly 4,300 residential properties and allowing up to 6 units per lot on approximately 600 properties. Secondary suites have been legal in all City single-family dwellings since 1993 — one suite per property, owner must reside at the property — and a suite may be combined with an accessory coach house, which requires a front lot line of at least 10 m (32.81 ft) plus a Development Permit and a Building Permit.

DISTRICT rules (29th Street north — Vista 29 / Churchill House block and the slope above): the District's Official Community Plan is Bylaw 7900; it designates Queensdale as a Village Centre and directs growth to its centres while preserving established low-density neighbourhoods, which covers the District portion of Upper Lonsdale. District zoning has permitted a principal dwelling, a secondary suite and a coach house — three units total — on single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary since June 2024. Slope is the defining hazard condition: the District designates Natural Hazard Development Permit Areas and publishes property-level GeoWeb hazard reports, so steep upper-Lonsdale lots should be checked before additions or rebuilds.

Taxes differ by side of the line: Both municipalities set 2026 property taxes due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty after July 2, 2026 and a further 5% after September 1, 2026. City 2026 residential total rate: 3.34028 per $1,000 of assessed value, plus a separate residential storm drainage rate of 0.10697 per $1,000. District 2026 residential total rate: 3.28195 per $1,000 (municipal portion 1.83419). Same street, different bills — confirm which municipality the specific unit is taxed in.

School district is the same on both sides: School District 44 (North Vancouver) serves both the City and District blocks — the municipal split does not change the school district, only the catchment, which is address-based.

blocks.text: Good to know about Upper Lonsdale

items.t: The whole 55+ cluster exists because one block was designated for it. The District's North Lonsdale–Delbrook Community Plan designated all of the 100 block of West Queens Road / West 29th Street for seniors' or empty-nester multi-family development at a maximum density of 36.3 units per acre — which is why the area's only three seniors buildings (Somerset Green just across the City line, Vista 29, and the assisted-living site that became the Churchill House block) all sit within a few hundred feet of each other at Queensdale, and why no other block in Upper Lonsdale has any.

Vista 29 was purpose-built as 55+, not converted. The District's Dec 22, 2004 report shows the project was designed from the start for ageing in place: units built to "Level 2" adaptable design guidelines (one suite to Level 3), wheelchair movement through doorways, kitchens and bathrooms, intruder alarms with panic buttons in the suites, corridor surveillance cameras, and facilities for charging scooters — with the 55+ occupancy covenant written into the rezoning.

Somerset Green has two addresses. The complex is listed as 121 West 29th St, but units are also addressed as 2800 Chesterfield Ave — a listing for 201–2800 Chesterfield Ave describes the same Somerset Green building. Searching only one address misses listings under the other.

Somerset Green's build year is not consistent across sources. Most current listings state 1987; at least one current listing states 1989. Its unit count in the District's 2004 report is 143 — a figure most listing copy never mentions.

The seniors' services anchor for the City-side blocks is brand new — and in Central Lonsdale, not here. The new Silver Harbour Seniors' Activity Centre at 2325 St Georges Ave, beside the new Harry Jerome Community Recreation Centre (main entrance 130 East 23rd St), opened July 25, 2026; the City records it as offering programs and services for adults 55+. It is a short trip down the hill from the 29th Street buildings, but it is not in Upper Lonsdale.

The District-side recreation anchor is the other direction. The Delbrook Community Recreation Centre at 851 West Queens Road is the North Vancouver Recreation & Culture centre serving the District blocks, with a main pool and a leisure pool plus indoor racquet facilities — west along Queens Road from the 29th Street cluster.

Slope rules, not just slope views, come with the upper blocks. The District designates Natural Hazard Development Permit Areas and publishes property-level GeoWeb hazard reports; on the steep streets above Queensdale, a geotechnical check can add cost to additions and rebuilds in a way the flat Central Lonsdale blocks never face.

The 29th Street tax difference is small but real, and it is permanent. For 2026 the City total residential rate is 3.34028 per $1,000 (plus 0.10697 storm drainage) against the District's 3.28195 — two otherwise comparable 55+ units across West 29th Street from each other are taxed by different municipalities at different rates, on the same July 2 due date.

faq.a: Two verified: Somerset Green, 121 West 29th St (143 units per a District council report; City side of 29th Street), and Vista 29, 188 West 29th St (50 units, plan BCS2494, built 2007; District side). Both appear on the North Shore list of buildings carrying a 55+ bylaw, and current listings for both state a 55+ occupancy rule.
faq.q: Which buildings in Upper Lonsdale can I actually buy into as 55+?

faq.a: No. Somerset Green is south of West 29th Street and is described in the District's own report as a seniors' condominium development "in the City of North Vancouver"; Vista 29 was rezoned by the District (CD 52) on the block between West Queens Road and West 29th Street. Different OCP, zoning bylaw, permit desk and tax rate apply to each — City total residential rate 3.34028 vs District 3.28195 per $1,000 for 2026.
faq.q: The two buildings face each other — are they in the same municipality?

faq.a: Only to live there. The Province states people under 55 can own a strata lot in a 55+ corporation but may not be able to reside in it; the bylaw applies to residents, not ownership.
faq.q: Do I have to be 55 to buy in a 55+ building, or only to live there?

faq.a: Yes — Strata Property Regulation 7.01 requires exemptions for a younger spouse/partner of a specified resident, a child under 19 in that resident's care, an adult child the resident cared for before age 19, live-in caregivers, and legacy residents who lived in the unit when the bylaw passed.
faq.q: Can my younger spouse or partner live with me in a 55+ strata?

faq.a: No — it has a second layer. The District's approval for the site included a restrictive covenant limiting occupancy to households where one member is 55 or older, in addition to the strata's own bylaws. Have both reviewed on a purchase.
faq.q: Is Vista 29's 55+ rule only a strata bylaw?

faq.a: No. It is a private-pay rental retirement residence at 150 West 29th St, registered with the Assisted Living Registry (operator Chartwell Master Care LP, class SN), offering independent living and assisted living in rental suites — not strata ownership.
faq.q: Is Chartwell Churchill House something I can buy?

faq.a: None verified. No Upper Lonsdale address appears as a subsidized seniors building in BC Housing's Zone 1 seniors directory (May 2025) in the sources checked; the Kiwanis subsidized buildings are in Central Lonsdale, Lower Lonsdale and Lynn Valley.
faq.q: Is there any subsidized or non-profit seniors rental in Upper Lonsdale?

faq.a: Somerset Green listings record an indoor pool, hot tub, workshop, gym, library, games room, lounge, courtyard gardens and 2 guest suites.
faq.q: What amenities do the two ownership buildings have?

faq.a: Route 230 buses run the full length of Lonsdale Avenue past the 29th Street block, down to Lonsdale Quay, where the SeaBus crosses to Waterfront Station in 12 minutes. For hospital access, Chartwell — in the same block as both strata buildings — states its residence is five minutes from Lions Gate Hospital.
faq.q: How do I get downtown or to the hospital without driving up and down the hill?

faq.a: Listings for both buildings describe them as pet friendly (Somerset Green listings also record cats OK in the listing data). The operative limit is each strata's registered bylaws — confirm the number/size rules on the Form B for the specific unit.
